summary: Customer reported a series of long-tail 5xx/timeout errors affecting checkout traffic during peak. Today alignment focused on containment (immediate fallback/rollback), investigation scope (logs, KV cache checks, prefix caching), and medium-term reliability mitigations (canary, circuit breaker, observability tweaks). SE and AE walked through a proposed rollback playbook, discussed tradeoffs between hosted failover vs Dedicated fallbacks, and agreed on short list of actions and timelines.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Lian Zhou (Redwood CSM), Jordan Reyes (BlueRidge SRE), Maya Patel (BlueRidge CTO), Harper Lee (Platform Eng), Diego Morales (BlueRidge Security)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on so quickly. I know this has been a pretty rough 36 hours for you, Jordan, so we appreciate the time. Quick agenda: containment/rollback, what we need from logs, and next steps.
[00:18] Jordan: Yeah thanks. Just to call it out again, the spikes started Friday evening kind of aligned with a batch job, but then spiked again Sunday at midnight. We saw a mix of 502/504s and a few "unknown token" responses that caused client retries.
[00:37] Maya: The business impact was significant — about 8% of checkout attempts saw increased latency and 1.2% failed end-to-end during the hour window. We're obviously worried about recurrence.
[00:54] Ethan: Quick clarifying question — when you say 502/504, is that upstream from our gateway or coming back from the model API? The traces Jordan shared had a couple of ambiguous spans.
[01:10] Jordan: Most look like model-side timeouts, but some appear to be in the KV cache layer — we saw a few cache miss storms. Also there's a chance our prefix caching wasn't hitting for longer sequences.
[01:29] Samira: Understood. We'll cover rollback options. Our immediate containment recommendations are: revert to the pinned model v1.3.2, increase short-circuit fallback rate to 20% to an earlier smaller model, and enable a strict circuit breaker on requests over 2.5s.
[01:48] Harper: Revert how? You mean on the Redwood side or in-app? We need a clear runbook. If it's Redwood-hosted that's easier, but if it's a Dedicated pool with pinned capacity we may need to do an app change.
[02:06] Ethan: Good question. For Hosted customers we can flip a routing flag and route to the pinned version (we did it for Acme last month), for Dedicated we can update the routing policy on the cluster but there may be a short propagation window. If you're on private, some customers have a control plane ACL that requires ops sign-off.
[02:28] Diego: Security concern — if we flip keys or route traffic, KMS key access patterns change. We have to ensure audit logs capture the rollback. Also need to confirm whether rollback touches PII retention flags.
[02:41] Samira: Noted. Diego, we'll include audit logging steps in the runbook. We'll also include a KMS check and a 'no PII persisted' validation step.
[02:56] Ethan: I'll run through the rollback steps now at a high level. Step 1: Stop routing to canary model. Step 2: Change routing to pinned v1.3.2 and enable fallback policy. Step 3: Warm KV cache with a controlled prefix to avoid miss storms. Step 4: Monitor token-level latencies and errors for 15 minutes.
[03:21] Maya: About warming the cache — is that something Redwood can kick off or do we need to push synthetic traffic? We don't want to inject artificial orders into prod.
[03:36] Ethan: We have a safe warming utility that hits the model with non-PII prompts to populate common prefixes. That can be run by Redwood ops. We'll share the script.
[03:48] Jordan: Please share. Also, we noticed a few spikes that correlated with a background batch that hits long sequences. Could sequence length distribution be pushing KV cache evictions?
[04:05] Ethan: Yes, long sequences can evict hot keys if cache sizes are tuned for median seq lengths. Part of the medium-term mitigation is tuning cache window and TTL.
[04:18] Harper: Is there any config we can change now to be less aggressive without a full deploy?
[04:25] Samira: We can lower the cache eviction threshold on the host for Dedicated pools in most cases, depending on GPU memory headroom. We'll check telemetry.
[04:37] [05:00] Lian: Quick note — I'll own communications for postmortem and customer-facing summary. Need a bullet list of what happened and timeline by tomorrow midday.
[05:10] Jordan: We'll get logs. The tricky bit is tying request IDs to model root cause; some of the spans are truncated.
[05:22] Ethan: Truncated spans — could be our tracer sampling thresholds. We can temporarily raise sampling for the affected routes to get full traces.
[05:33] Jordan: Okay do that.
[05:40] [06:12] Maya: I also want to understand the root cause possibilities — is this a regression in the model, a runtime scheduling problem, or a workload change?
[06:25] Ethan: At this point it's a mix. There was a recent model variant rollout last week that introduced a change in response length distribution; that can increase KV pressure. Also there were a couple of infra-level preempt events around the same time, which could cause increased latency.
[06:44] Samira: We'll treat investigation as parallel tracks: model telemetries (token lengths, response size), runtime (OOM/preempt logs), and cache metrics (miss ratio, eviction rate).
[06:58] Jordan: Can you also map which customers hit the Dedicated pool vs Hosted? Some traffic crosses both and we need to know scope.
[07:10] Samira: Yes, we have that mapping. We'll include it in the artifact bundle.
[07:18] [08:00] Diego: On compliance — we need to make sure any rollback won't violate our data residency settings. If you route to a different region model variant that may change residency.
[08:12] Ethan: Good call. Our rollback recommendation keeps region constant; it's purely a model version swap, not region change, so residency should remain intact.
[08:26] Harper: About the circuit breaker, what thresholds are we suggesting and how do we avoid false positives? We've seen circuit breakers trip during legitimate traffic surges.
[08:39] Samira: We're proposing a 2.5s latency ceiling and a 25% error rate window over 60s for automatic short-circuit. For initial containment we'll set it to conservative values and then tighten based on observed telemetry.
[08:58] [09:30] Jordan: For the logs we'll share three representative request IDs that hit failures, plus the full span traces around them. Expect these to be in S3 under blue-ridge-ops/logs/2025-12-17.
[09:45] Ethan: Perfect. Once we have those request IDs we'll correlate against token-level logs and kernel selection traces to see if a slow kernel path or quantization mismatch triggered a slowdown.
[09:59] Maya: Any mention of model quantization? We did run a quantized variant for cost reasons in the last deploy window.
[10:10] Ethan: Yes you mentioned quantization — if there's a quantization mismatch for certain sequence shapes it can degrade perf. We'll check which kernel was selected for the failing spans. Sometimes the runtime picks a slower CPU fallback if GPU memory is fragmented.
[10:28] Samira: That's a great point — we'll include kernel selection metadata in what we collect.
[10:35] [11:00] Lian: For the postmortem doc I need: timeline, impact (KPI numbers), mitigation steps, root cause hypotheses, decisions and owners. I'll draft an initial doc and send by EOD tomorrow.
[11:16] Jordan: We'll provide the timeline and logs by Friday.
[11:22] [12:00] Harper: Could we also enable a canary split for 5% of non-critical traffic to test the warm-up approach?
[12:10] Ethan: Yes, can do a canary. We recommend controlled canary with full tracing and increased sampling, then scale up if stable.
[12:21] Maya: Are there any longer-term reliability improvements you recommend? We'd like to avoid manual rollbacks every time.
[12:30] Samira: Longer term: automated health-based routing with progressive rollouts (A/B to a small set, automated rollback on SLOs), improved KV cache sizing auto-tuning, token-level adaptive batching to reduce tail latency, and more comprehensive canary tests for sequence-length extremes.
[12:52] Ethan: Also invest in a "fallback fleet" — a small, cheaper model pool that's always warm for hard fallbacks to avoid cold startup penalties. That helps with both latency and cost in a pinch.
[13:06] Diego: We need to make sure the fallback fleet doesn't leak logs or increase retention beyond our retention policy.
[13:15] Samira: We'll document that; fallback fleet will use same retention & encryption settings.
[13:25] [14:00] Jordan: One weird thing — a few traces show the annotation "red wood dedicated" in the spans — transcription artifact but also we sometimes see naming inconsistencies in the telemetry which makes hunts harder. Any plan to standardize span names?
[14:39] Ethan: We're working to standardize service names and span tags. We'll push a naming guideline and add a small adapter to map legacy tags.
[14:55] [15:30] Samira: Recap of immediate commitments: Redwood to share rollback runbook draft (Samira), Redwood SE to run cache warm-up script and bench tests (Ethan), BlueRidge to provide 3 representative request IDs and logs (Jordan), Security check on KMS and audit before rollback (Diego).
[15:56] Maya: Timeline check — can we aim to perform the rollback tomorrow morning 2025-12-19 during a low-traffic window if all artifacts are ready?
[16:08] Samira: We can aim for that, subject to us getting logs and your sign-off on the runbook. We'll prepare an operations checklist and send for sign-off.
[16:22] Lian: I'll prepare the customer-facing incident summary once we have the initial timeline and will coordinate internal comms.
[16:33] Ethan: One more technical note — we recommend increasing tracer sampling for affected endpoints to 100% for a 2h window post-rollback to verify error rates. Expect additional log volume, so plan S3 retention temporarily.
[16:51] Diego: We'll sign off but need to check storage quotas; will confirm.
[17:02] Samira: Great. Any other questions?
[17:10] Jordan: No, that's it for now. Thanks all.
[17:18] Maya: Thanks — appreciate the quick cadence.
[17:25] End meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-labels and crosstalk; some proper nouns transcribed oddly ("red wood" for Redwood, "K V cache" for KV cache).
